A 48-year-old man seeks urological consultation for erectile dysfunction, reporting inability to achieve
adequate erection for penetration. His medical history includes a 20-year gap in physician visits,
current smoking habit of 1.5 packs daily, and well-managed major depressive disorder treated with
fluoxetine. Vital signs show temperature 98.1°F, blood pressure 137/82 mmHg, pulse 72/min, and
respiratory rate 12/min. Physical examination reveals an uncircumcised penis with normal meatus and
bilaterally descended testes. Laboratory results show normal thyroid-stimulating hormone and
testosterone levels. Nocturnal penile tumescence testing yields normal results. What is the most
probable underlying cause of this patient's erectile dysfunction? Answer Choices: (A) Psychogenic (B)
Mixed organic-psychogenic (C) Vascular (D) Medication-induced (E) Age-related (F) Endocrine (G)
Neurologic (H) Pharmacologic (I) Anatomic (J) Lifestyle-induced
 A. Anatomic
B. Vascular
C. Psychogenic
D. Medication-induced
E. Age-related
F. Lifestyle-induced
G. Pharmacologic
H. Endocrine
I. Mixed organic-psychogenic
J. Neurologic
